name: Community of Portuguese Language Countries (CPLP)
description: A white field with a blue border, charged at the centre with the CPLP emblem — a circle of blue wave shapes around a concentric ring — above the letters 'CPLP' in blue.
history: The Community of Portuguese Language Countries was founded in Lisbon on 17 July 1996 by Angola, Brazil, Cape Verde, Guinea-Bissau, Mozambique, Portugal and São Tomé and Príncipe; East Timor joined in 2002 and Equatorial Guinea in 2014. The emblem's wave shapes originally counted the founders and were not revised as membership grew.

features.symbolism: the sea, the first bond between the Portuguese-speaking peoples; the waves stand for the founding members
